decisions.reason: Report designs paste_image.png / paste_file.<ext> with (2),(3)... numbering before the extension until a free name is found, reserves names within the batch (numbering continues across items in one add(), validateItems run after renaming) and across live attachments, scopes renaming to the paste path only (drop and picker keep item.path verbatim, with an origin:'paste' gate inside add() offered as equivalent), and grounds everything in add()/validateItems/label from plugin-attachment-flow.js.

Report names input.state.getSnapshot().occurrences as the authoritative taken-name source, supplements it with in-flight records entries, and explains the fixture's alive-subscription deletes records.delete(ref) on any momentary empty snapshot while the attachment stays live, so a records-only set under-reports and numbering silently restarts.

Report uses tags-api-response.txt (x-cache: HIT, age 178, list showing only v0.2.9/v0.2.8/v0.2.7 while git ls-remote shows v0.2.10/v0.2.11 exist) plus renderCurrentChip(tag) printing the fetched tag, and prescribes semantic comparison fetched vs PLUGIN_VERSION: update chip only when remote is newer; otherwise display the running version, never the older fetched tag.

Report proposes concrete tests with expected names/assertions: multi-item single-batch paste yields paste_image.png and paste_image(2).png; a paste with an emptied records Map still blocks the live name and yields paste_image(2).png; drop/picker names stay verbatim; and chip tests for older (v0.2.9 vs 0.2.10), equal (v0.2.10) and newer (v0.2.11) remote tags.

Report requires syncing the hand-inlined PLUGIN_VERSION in lib/client.js with package.json (suggesting a drift gate), node --check on the bundle plus behavioral regressions, and explains deployment is manual reinstall/copy of the lib artifact followed by restart/refresh, noting the chip cannot install updates and there is no host-side update endpoint — grounded in the fixture's lib-only, no-build-step design.
